plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In such auctions, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy: bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth, while bidding lower reduces my chances of winning profitable auctions without changing what I'd pay if I win. Since my value is $24, I will bid exactly $24 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so there's no benefit to shading my bid up or down. My value is $9, so I'll bid exactly that. If I win, I pay less than $9 (whatever the second-highest bid is), guaranteeing non-negative profit. If I lose, I pay nothing and lose nothing.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the optimal (weakly dominant) strategy. If I bid my true value of $13, I win whenever the second-highest bid is below $13, paying that second-highest bid, ensuring non-negative profit. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value.
